🔤 Teaching reading and numbers at the kitchen table Reading with McGuffey (McGuffey Readers): 1. Start with the Primer: "Only about six new words are to be mastered in each lesson", and you can teach by sounds (phonics), by whole words, by the alphabet, or a mix. The script lessons and "slate exercises" at the back teach writing too (p. 7). 2. Then the First Reader. Phonics way: teach the sounds of the letters in the lesson, then put them together into words; words way: learn the words at the top of the lesson by sight and read without stopping; best is both, words first, then sounds and spelling. Teach writing letters along with their names (p. 6). 3. Second and Third Readers for children reading on their own; the Third has a lesson on reading with expression to practise aloud (Third Reader, p. 14). Numbers with Ray's: 1. Count real things first. "Movable objects are better for exercises in counting than pictures": marbles, beans, kernels of corn, or pebbles (Ray's Primary, p. 11). 2. Then the sums to 20, written out on a slate so they don't count on their fingers. "Teach one thing at a time, and teach it thoroughly" (same page). Lesson 1: point to each ball and count, then write the figure (p. 12). 3. Mental arithmetic in Ray's Intellectual needs no paper and teaches a

it thoroughly" (same page). Lesson 1: point to each ball and count, then write the figure (p. 12). 3. Mental arithmetic in Ray's Intellectual needs no paper and teaches a child "to reason, to analyze, to think for himself" (p. 9). Written arithmetic goes on in Ray's Practical; worked answers for parents are in the Key. Older children teach younger ones. Structured tutoring works better than now-and-then help; short runs (up to about four weeks) on basic skills give the best results, math most of all, then reading (Peer Tutoring, p. 18). A child a few years older often sees what a learner doesn't understand better than an adult does (p. 19). Keep lessons short, 15-20 minutes for young children, and stop while it is still going well (rule of thumb). 🗣 Telling stories with no book From Sara Cone Bryant's How to Tell Stories to Children (1905): 1. Pick a story with action, a little mystery and some repetition, like The Three Bears or The Three Little Pigs (p. 76). 2. "Know your story." Don't learn it word for word: memorizing "utterly destroys the freedom" of telling. Tell it over and over out loud to an imaginary listener until it flows, keeping only the best phrases of the original (pp. 118-121). 3. Seat little children close, in a half-circle, with you opposite the middle and no child behind another: "Little children have to be physically close in order to be mentally close" (p. 122). 4. Be natural. No sugary voice (p. 125); "short, familiar, vivid words"; keep the story moving and end it "with a snap" (p. 127). There's "no need to speak loudly" (p. 136). 5. Tired of the story? "Make believe" you enjoy it; the real interest usually comes back (p. 133). 6. Afterwards let them retell it, draw it, or play it: "Who would like to be Red Ridinghood?" (p. 144). The book's second half is stories ready to tell, sorted by age: for the youngest The Cooky, The Pied Piper, The Star Dollars; for 7-8 The Cat and the Parrot, The Fire-Bringer, Little Daylight; for 9-10 Arthur and the Sword, Why the Sea is Salt, The

Cooky, The Pied Piper, The Star Dollars; for 7-8 The Cat and the Parrot, The Fire-Bringer, Little Daylight; for 9-10 Arthur and the Sword, Why the Sea is Salt, The Little Hero of Haarlem (contents, pp. 16-17). Your own stories count most. Tell how grandparents lived, how the family came to the valley, what you did as a child; let children make up endings and tell the next part (rule of thumb). A child who can't talk about what happened may "draw a picture or tell a story of what happened" (FEMA, p. 189).

🏃 Group and outdoor games Pick games for the age (Bancroft, pp. 27-28): about 6 years, games with lots of repetition, pretending to be animals or farmers, and one chaser after one runner; two or three years later, catching a whole group, daring, choosing sides; from 11-12, harder races and team play. How to run a game (Bancroft, pp. 41-42): - Explain the whole game before anyone plays; walk a few players through it slowly. "Never try to teach and play a game at the same time." - Too many players means bored players: split into smaller groups, and make the rowdiest older children the group leaders. 🧶 String figures: cat's cradle and more The string: about 6 ft long, ends tied to make a loop about 3 ft long. A woven cord kinks less than a twisted one; tie the ends in a small square knot (Jayne, p. 36). Most figures start with the hands in the "usual position": palms facing each other, fingers pointing up (same page). First Position (p. 42): 1. Put both little fingers in the loop and pull the hands apart. 2. Turn the palms away from you, put each thumb into the little-finger loop from below, pick up the near string on the back of the thumb, turn the palms to face each other again and pull tight. Opening A, which starts more than half of all string figures (pp. 43-44): 1. First Position. 2. Put the right index finger up under the string that crosses the left palm, and pull the hands apart (Fig. 12). 3. Put the left index finger up under the string crossing the right palm, between the strings on the right index, and pull apart (Fig. 13). Now there is a loop on each thumb, index and little finger (Fig. 14). Always right first, then left (p. 44). Opening A: right index first (Fig. 12), then left (Fig. 13), and the finished opening (Fig. 14) (Jayne, pp. 43-44). Osage Diamonds, also called Jacob's Ladder (pp. 60,

Opening A. 2. Drop the thumb loops and pull the hands apart. 3. Each thumb goes away from you under all the strings and picks up the far little-finger string from below. 4. Each thumb goes away from you over the near index string and picks up the far index string from below. 5. Drop the little-finger loops and pull apart. 6. Each little finger goes toward you over the near index string and picks up the far thumb string from below. 7. Drop the thumb loops. 8. Put each index finger down into the little triangle by the thumb, turn the palms down, drop the little-finger loops, pull apart and turn the palms away from you: the diamonds appear (Fig. 50). ✏ Pencil, paper and word games All from Bancroft unless noted; most need only voices. - Buzz: count around the circle, but say "Buzz" for 7, any multiple of 7, and any number with a 7 in it; a mistake starts it again at one (p. 254). - Beast, Bird or Fish: throw a knotted handkerchief at someone, call "Bird!" and count to ten; they must name a bird not named before (p. 253). - What Is My Thought Like? One person thinks of a thing, everyone guesses what it is "like", then each must say why the thought is like their answer, however silly (p. 280). - Crambo: everyone writes a question on one slip and a noun on another; mix them, draw one of each, and write a verse that answers the question and uses the word (p. 256). - Naughts and Crosses (tic-tac-toe) on a slate, paper or the ground (p. 269). - What Will You Take to the Picnic? Only the host knows the secret rule (the food must start with the guest's initial); the others must work it out (Girls' Handy Book, p. 178). - Shadow Verbs: act out a verb as a shadow on a sheet lit from behind, and the others guess it (Girls' Handy Book, p. 180). Keep the lamp on a steady base well away from the sheet (rule of thumb).

✂ Things to make Corn-husk dolls (Mother Nature's Toy-Shop, pp. 166-168): 1. Use the soft inner husks, about two per doll; soak brittle ones in water. 2. Lay one husk partly over the other, fold across the middle, fold the sides to the back, and wind soft string round for the neck and head (Fig. 186), then lower down for the waist (Fig. 187). 3. For arms, roll a husk lengthwise, trim the ends, and tie it at the middle and near each end (Fig. 188). 4. An adult pushes a small knife blade through the shoulders; slide the arms in along the flat of the blade. 5. For a boy doll, split the skirt and tie each half into a leg (Fig. 189). Head and neck, waist, arms, and the finished doll (Mother Nature's Toy-Shop, pp. 167-168). 🎭 Making your own books, plays and newspapers - Books: paper, ink, pens, slates and keeping books dry are in the Paper & Ink guide. For little hands, a cloth book of strong linen or colored cambric lasts (Girls' Handy Book, p. 417); for any home-made book, two pieces of heavy cardboard with three holes near the edge, laced or tied through matching holes in the pages (p. 423). - Children's own books: each child writes and draws a story, a record of the year, the family tree, or a guide to the plants and birds around the house; read them aloud on a show night (rule of thumb). - Play the story: after a story is told, hand out the parts and act it; in a little company "it is an all-star cast, and no one realizes any indignity in a subordinate role" (Bryant, p. 144). - A puppet theater: an old picture frame about 2 ft by 18 in with white muslin tacked on the back makes the stage (Boys' Handy Book, p. 347), and the book has a whole puppet play of Puss in Boots (p. 358). Put the light on a steady base, well back from the cloth (rule of thumb). - A family "paper" or club: the Literary Sketch Club picks a subject; members bring a song, a sketch, a poem or an essay about

🕯 Light for reading, and fire safety around children - One small light, everyone close: with aluminum foil on three sides and the bottom of a small lamp, hung between you and the book, a flame "smaller than that of a birthday candle" is enough to read by, and shelter families "will appreciate having someone read aloud to them" (Kearny, p. 104). Do crafts and lessons by daylight near a window and save lamp fuel for story time (rule of thumb). - Where the lamp sits: a safe lamp is short and heavy with flat sides so it won't roll; never at the edge of a table; don't hang lamps on walls; never add fuel to a burning lamp (WHO, p. 106). "Keep lamps and matches out of reach of children" (Where There Is No Doctor, p. 22). - Before sleep, every flame out. Carbon monoxide has no color or smell; "unconsciousness and death can occur without warning" (FM 21-76, p. 182). - No flame inside paper or cloth: no candles in paper lanterns, tents, puppet screens or blanket forts (rule of thumb). No outdoor fires for fun in fire season, June to October; see the Wildfire guide. - A small burn: clean cool water (not ice) right away, for no longer than 20 minutes; "Never put ice, grease, fat" on a burn (Where There Is No Doctor, p. 22).

🌙 A simple evening routine A plan that works in most homes (rule of thumb, built on FEMA, p. 189 and SPR, p. 101: routine, meals together, time at bedtime). Move it earlier in winter, when it is dark by 5. 1. Before dark: evening chores done together: water, wood, animals shut in, lamps filled by an adult. 2. Supper together, at the table, same time each day. Each person tells one good thing from the day. 3. Game time, 30-45 minutes: cards, a board game, string figures, or a quiet game everyone can play. 4. A song or two, a round if there are enough voices. 5. Story time: a chapter read aloud by the one lamp, or a told story for the little ones. 6. Bed: a few minutes with each child; this is when worries come out. Then every flame out. Once a week, a show night: a puppet show, a play, poems recited from McGuffey, a reading from someone's own book, a song from each person. In summer, play outside until dusk and save lamp fuel (rule of thumb).

Fly kites by day | | A paper lantern on a kite's tail, "the Moving Star", which "the motion of the kite is apt to set fire to" (Boys', p. 41) | No flame on a kite, ever | | Candles inside paper lanterns hung on wires and trees, and in cloth or paper "illuminated tents" (Girls' Handy Book, p. 133) | No flame in paper or cloth. Recommended Routine Immunizations for Children - Table 2 (WHO Dec 2025). WHO's current childhood vaccine schedule: which vaccines, age of first dose, gaps between doses. WHO, free download. In Medical / Childbirth-Children / Child-Health.

World Report on Child Injury Prevention - Drowning Burns Falls Poisoning (WHO UNICEF 2008). Thinking Healthy - Psychosocial Management of Perinatal Depression (WHO 2015). Step-by-step home sessions a trained neighbor can use to help a depressed pregnant or new mother, with no medicines and no specialist. WHO all rights reserved, free download. In Medical / Childbirth-Children / Mothers.

Caring for the Newborn at Home - Community Health Worker Participant Manual (WHO UNICEF 2015). WHO all rights reserved, free download. In Medical / Childbirth-Children / Newborn.

Infant and Young Child Feeding - Model Chapter 2nd ed (WHO 2025). Current WHO reference on breastfeeding problems: is the baby getting enough, low milk, sore or flat nipples, engorgement, blocked ducts, mastitis, thrush. Also first foods and feeding in emergencies. CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO. In Medical / Childbirth-Children / Newborn.

Parent Counselling Guide on Kangaroo Mother Care - Skin-to-Skin for Small Babies (WHO 2025). Picture guide for parents of early or small babies: how many hours of skin-to-skin, how to position and tie the baby on, feeding every 2-3 hours, warning signs. CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO. In Medical / Childbirth-Children / Newborn.

Managing Complications in Pregnancy and Childbirth 2nd ed (WHO 2017). WHO guide for midwives and doctors: heavy bleeding after birth (womb compression, aortic compression), breech, stuck shoulders, eclampsia, infection. CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO. In Medical / Field-Care / Childbirth-Newborn.

Pregnancy Childbirth Postpartum and Newborn Care - Guide for Essential Practice 3rd ed (WHO 2015). In Medical / Field-Care / Childbirth-Newborn.

Promoting Oral Health in Africa - Basic Package of Oral Care and Urgent Treatment Protocols (WHO AFRO 2016). Decontamination and Reprocessing of Medical Devices for Health-care Facilities (WHO-PAHO 2016). Cleaning, disinfecting and sterilizing instruments (steam, dry heat, chemicals) and why boiling is not sterilization. WHO all rights reserved, free download. In Medical / Field-Care / Nursing-Care.

Hospital Corpsman Nonresident Training Course NAVEDTRA 14295 (US Navy 2000). Navy medic textbook: patient assessment and vital signs, post-op and orthopedic care, making and splitting casts, emergency childbirth, diet, emergency dental care. Nursing Interventions Wound Care and Splint Management in Prolonged Casualty Care CPG 70 (Joint Trauma System 2025). In Medical / Field-Care / Nursing-Care.

Treatment of Diarrhoea - Manual for Physicians and Other Senior Health Workers (WHO 2005). ATP 4-02.11 Casualty Response Tactical Combat Casualty Care and First Aid (US Army 2026). Distribution A, public domain. In Medical / Field-Care / Trauma-Bleeding.

First Aid in Armed Conflicts and Other Situations of Violence (ICRC 2006). Red Cross manual for first aiders where hospitals are far or unsafe: scene safety, triage, bleeding, airway, when CPR is useless, moving casualties. In Medical / Field-Care / Trauma-Bleeding.

Hypothermia Prevention Monitoring and Management CPG 23 (Joint Trauma System 2023). Keeping injured, bleeding and burned people warm: insulation from the ground, wet clothing, vapor barriers, safe use of heat packs. Public domain. In Medical / Field-Care / Trauma-Bleeding.

Prolonged Casualty Care Guidelines CPG 91 (Joint Trauma System 2021). What to do hour by hour when evacuation is delayed or impossible: re-checking and converting tourniquets, shock, oral fluids, infection, monitoring. US government, public domain. In Medical / Field-Care / Trauma-Bleeding.

WHO-ICRC Basic Emergency Care - Approach to the Acutely Ill and Injured (WHO 2018). ABCDE check of any sick or hurt person, trauma, breathing trouble, shock, confusion, burns chart, recovery position, splinting, spine care. CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO. In Medical / Field-Care / Trauma-Bleeding.

Acute Traumatic Wound Management in Prolonged Field Care CPG 62 (Joint Trauma System 2017). Irrigation volumes and water choice, when to close or leave open, bites, infection, and an appendix on sterilizing instruments with a pressure cooker, oven, bleach or boiling. Public domain. Burn Wound Management in Prolonged Field Care CPG 57 (Joint Trauma System 2017). Sizing burns, drinking-based fluid replacement when there is no IV, urine targets, blisters, daily dressing care, pain control. Public domain. In Medical / Field-Care / Wounds-Burns-Fractures.

Sepsis Management in Prolonged Field Care CPG 83 (Joint Trauma System 2020). Spotting an infection that has spread to the whole body (fever, fast pulse and breathing, confusion) before blood pressure falls, and what to do. Public domain. In Medical / Field-Care / Wounds-Burns-Fractures.

Snakebite Envenomation CPG 81 (Joint Trauma System 2026). Current snakebite care incl. North American rattlesnakes: what to do, and the outdated first aid (bands, cutting, suction, ice) that must not be done. Public domain. In Medical / Field-Care / Wounds-Burns-Fractures.

Spider and Scorpion Envenomation CPG 84 (Joint Trauma System 2026). Black widow and recluse-type bites: signs, pain control, wound care, what not to do. Public domain. In Medical / Field-Care / Wounds-Burns-Fractures.

Surgical Care at the District Hospital (WHO 2003). WHO all rights reserved, free download. In Medical / Field-Care / Wounds-Burns-Fractures.

War Surgery - Working with Limited Resources Vol 1 (ICRC 2010). In Medical / Field-Care / Wounds-Burns-Fractures.

Emergency War Surgery 5th US Revision 2018. Borden Institute (US Army) Emergency War Surgery, 5th US Revision 2018: all 37 chapters plus index in one 620-page PDF; trauma, burns, wounds, field surgery (public domain). In Medical / Manuals-PDF.

MSF Clinical Guidelines - Diagnosis and Treatment Manual. Medecins Sans Frontieres "Clinical guidelines - diagnosis and treatment manual" (English, 409 pages, exported 30/01/2025): symptoms, diagnosis and treatment with doses for common diseases. In Medical / Manuals-PDF.

(PHS) 03-2024), 412 pages including a 2-page Public.Resource.Org cover sheet; first aid and medicine-chest drug guide for crews with no doctor (public domain). In Medical / Manuals-PDF.

Special Forces Medical Handbook ST 31-91B 1982. US Army ST 31-91B Special Forces Medical Handbook (1 March 1982), searchable scan; austere diagnosis and treatment; its drug information is now outdated (public domain). In Medical / Manuals-PDF.
Where There Is No Dentist. Dental care without a dentist. In Medical / Manuals-PDF.

In Medical / Medicinal-Plants.

WHO Monographs on Selected Medicinal Plants Vol 1. WHO monographs on selected medicinal plants, Volume 1 (1999): evidence, uses, doses, contraindications and adverse effects of 28 plants. In Medical / Medicinal-Plants.
WHO Monographs on Selected Medicinal Plants Vol 2. WHO monographs on selected medicinal plants, Volume 2 (2002); the scan starts at the Introduction (no cover page). In Medical / Medicinal-Plants.
WHO Monographs on Selected Medicinal Plants Vol 3. WHO monographs on selected medicinal plants, Volume 3 (2007). In Medical / Medicinal-Plants.
WHO Monographs on Selected Medicinal Plants Vol 4. WHO monographs on selected medicinal plants, Volume 4 (2009). In Medical / Medicinal-Plants.
FDA Drug Disposal Options Flowchart 2024. FDA one-page flowchart (Sept 2024): take-back, flush list, or household-trash disposal of unwanted medicines. In Medical / Medicines.

FDA How to Dispose of Unused Medicines 2013. FDA consumer sheet (Dec 2013) on disposing of medicines in household trash or by flushing; its flush list is outdated but the method still applies. In Medical / Medicines.

MSF Essential Drugs - Practical Guidelines. Medecins Sans Frontieres "Essential drugs - practical guidelines" (663 pages, exported 28/04/2026): drug-by-drug indications, doses, contraindications, side effects, storage. In Medical / Medicines.

Stability of Medicines Beyond Expiry Dates - Zilker 2019. University of Wuerzburg doctoral thesis (2019, 146 pages) reviewing SLEP and testing decades-old expired drugs: which medicines keep potency and which degrade. In Medical / Medicines.
WHO Model Formulary 2008. WHO Model Formulary 2008 (644 pages): uses, doses, contraindications, side effects and interactions of the essential medicines. In Medical / Medicines.
WHO Model Formulary for Children 2010. WHO Model Formulary for Children 2010 (528 pages): children's doses (0-12 years), cautions and side effects of essential medicines. In Medical / Medicines.
WHO Model List of Essential Medicines 24th List 2025. WHO Model List of Essential Medicines, 24th list (2025): the core medicines and strengths a health system should stock. In Medical / Medicines.
WHO Model List of Essential Medicines for Children 10th List 2025. WHO Model List of Essential Medicines for Children, 10th list (2025). In Medical / Medicines.

Chair Rise Exercise - STEADI (CDC 2017). CDC one-page leg-strength exercise for weak or older adults: sit-to-stand 10-15 times, two sets. In Medical / Rehab-Physical-Therapy.

FM 7-22 Army Physical Readiness Training - Reconditioning (US Army 2012). US Army 2012 fitness manual; ch. 6 reconditioning after injury: walk-to-run table, hip and shoulder drills, return advice for knee, ankle, back and shoulder. In Medical / Rehab-Physical-Therapy.

Managing Low Back Pain - Patient Booklet (VA DoD 2022). VA/DoD booklet: stay active not bed rest, moist heat, pelvic rock, cat/camel, knee-to-chest, getting out of bed, red flags. In Medical / Rehab-Physical-Therapy.

Postural Hypotension - Dizziness on Standing - STEADI (CDC 2017). CDC sheet on dizziness on standing (after bed rest, dehydration, medicines): get up in stages, pump the feet, hold on, drink. In Medical / Rehab-Physical-Therapy.

Recovering from a Mild Traumatic Brain Injury or Concussion (CDC 2024). CDC patient sheet: concussion symptoms, danger signs, light activity then exercise, gradual return to work, heights and machinery. In Medical / Rehab-Physical-Therapy.

TM 8-292 Physical Reconditioning (US Army 1952). US Army 1952 reconditioning manual: harmful effects of bed rest, bed exercises with drawings, conditioning for crutch walking (old; check against newer sources). In Medical / Rehab-Physical-Therapy.

Mathematics Vol 1 - Arithmetic to Geometry and Trigonometry (US Navy NavPers 10069-C 1966). NRCS Construction Surveying and Quantity Computations - NEH Part 645 Ch 5 (USDA NRCS 2012). NRCS Engineering Field Handbook Ch 1 - Surveying (USDA NRCS 2022). FM 5-34 Engineer Field Data (US Army 1987). NIST Handbook 44 Appendix C - General Tables of Units of Measurement (NIST 2024).
